Package game.status

Class TimedStatus

java.lang.Object
game.status.TimedStatus
All Implemented Interfaces:
Status
Direct Known Subclasses:
BurningStatus, DroughtWearinessStatus, GrowthPausedStatus, IncapacitatingStatus, StrawberryHealStatus, StrawberryPoisonStatus
public abstract class TimedStatus extends Object implements Status
A Status whose effect is applied once per turn for a fixed number of turns, then expires on its own.

This is the shared shape behind every timed, self-expiring status in the game (healing, poison, burning, and similar): count down a fixed number of turns, applying one subclass-specific effect each turn, and report the status as inactive once the count reaches zero. Subclasses only need to say what the per-turn effect is and how many turns it lasts; the counting itself is implemented here exactly once.

    • tickStatus

      public final void tickStatus(GameEntity currentEntity, Location location)
      Applies one turn's worth of this status's effect, then decrements the remaining duration. The counting is identical for every timed status, so it is implemented here once and sealed with final; subclasses only supply applyEffect(), and may describe the turn through describeTurn(Location), which is printed when it is not empty.
      Specified by:
      tickStatus in interface Status
      Parameters:
      currentEntity - the entity this status is attached to
      location - the location of the entity this status is attached to
      See Also:

    • describeTurn

      protected String describeTurn(Location location)
      Describes what this status did on the turn just applied, so that an effect the player cannot otherwise see is reported. By default a status says nothing; a status whose effect should be visible overrides this.
      Parameters:
      location - the location of the entity this status is attached to
      Returns:
      a description of this turn's effect, or an empty string to print nothing

    • replaceOn

      public final void replaceOn(Actor actor)
      Attaches this status to the given Actor, first removing any status of the same concrete type the Actor already carries.

      This is for statuses that should not stack (e.g. a fresh Burn resets the clock on an old one rather than adding a second, independent Burn). A status that is meant to stack instead (healing, poison) is simply added directly with actor.addStatus(...) and does not call this method.

      Parameters:
      actor - the Actor to attach this status to
